input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale:
Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer, which fails the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and cannot sit at the fallback (early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) because it is a payment-delay charge rather than a termination fee. At fifteen percent of annual Fees per week, triggered by a ten-day payment delay, it would exceed the remaining contract value within roughly seven weeks — walk-away territory. No other Customer-payable liquidated amount appears (termination in Sections 9.4 and 10 has none), and the SLA credits running to us are beneficial and not flagged. The redline flips the operator so that no liquidated damages and no penalty are payable by Customer, leaving Vendor's other late-payment remedies and Section 7.3 untouched.</rationale>
